0.description: Sample additionalProperty entries (base AdditionalProperty shape). The XDI Sample.* propertyID vocabulary enum is layered on in xasOptional, so it applies at the profile level, not this shape.

properties.description: Entities the activity used. Optional. Each item is a string (an IRI or a free-text name) or an object that identifies the entity by @id. The @id reference is deliberately NOT sealed: an extending profile may describe the entity in place as long as it keeps the @id, and a profile that wants only bare references can seal it itself. Role-keyed wrappers (an object whose key names a role, with no @id) are not accepted; in the schema.org implementation what an activity used is recorded with schema:instrument and schema:object instead.

Instruments, software and reagents the activity used. Each item is either an {@id} reference to a thing described elsewhere, or a description in place whose schema:additionalType carries exactly one of three Wikidata terms (as the Wikidata entity IRI https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q..., or a wd: CURIE bound to it), which says what kind of thing it is and selects the shape it must have: https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q3099911 (measuring instrument) -> Instrument; https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7397 (software) -> Software; https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q2356542 (chemical reagent, used here for reagents and reference materials) -> Reagent. The kind is read from additionalType, not @type, because a reagent can be a schema:Product just as an instrument is. Always an array: one activity commonly uses several (a laser ablation cell plus the ICP-MS it feeds, the acquisition software, the standards).
Human-readable name for the activity
Text description of what this activity did
Formal identifier for this activity
Primary responsible agent for this activity (maps to PROV wasAssociatedWith)
Other participants in this activity

Input entity (or entities) for this activity. Per schema.org, the range of schema:object is schema:Thing. Accepts four shapes (1) a string URI, (2) an @id reference object, (3) an inline schema:Thing object, or (4) an array whose items take any of those shapes (used when an activity has multiple inputs, e.g. samples analyzed). Supports action chaining where the value references the result of a prior activity.

Output entity (or entities) produced by this activity. Per schema.org, the range is schema:Thing. Accepts: (1) a string URI reference (action chaining shorthand to be referenced as schema:object of a subsequent activity); (2) a single {"@id": "<uri>"} object reference; (3) an inline schema:Thing (object with @type); or (4) an array of any of these forms (e.g. multiple datasets produced by this activity). Profiles may restrict the array item shape further.
Status of this activity
ISO8601 date-time when the activity started (maps to PROV startedAtTime)
ISO8601 date-time when the activity ended (maps to PROV endedAtTime)
Where the activity occurred

The plan the activity followed, or the procedure as it was performed. The {@id} reference form is the link to the plan (a protocol, method or workflow definition described elsewhere; CDIF defines no inline plan object). An inline HowTo is the procedure as performed; when the activity also followed a plan, that HowTo links the plan with schema:isBasedOn. One path finds the plan in both cases: prov:wasGeneratedBy/schema:actionProcess/schema:isBasedOn?
Error description for failed activities

Domain-specific extension properties, typically the parameter values this run used. schema.org does not list Action among this property's domains, so validator.schema.org warns on it; that warning is known and accepted, because schema.org has no Action property for parameter values.
Domain type(s) for the activity; must include xas:analysisevent (an XAS analysis event).

Must classify the place as an XAS facility. The value is a sealed reference ({"@id": ...}) per the CDIF convention for a term defined elsewhere; the core block also permits a bare string or an inline DefinedTerm for other classifications carried alongside this one.
Facility-scope properties that are not places, e.g. storage-ring energy or current. Not offered by the core block, which describes a location rather than an operating machine.
Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.
Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.
Note for editors and maintainers.
Note documenting a change.
Note about past state or use.
General note about this concept.
Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.
Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.
Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).
Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.
A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.
the identifier string. E.g. 10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
text label for the term that is useful to human user
Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.
Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.
Reference back to the instrument @id.
Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments), each naming how the target relates to the instrument. Uses the same linkRole block as cdifCore; before 2026-09-23 this property was a labeled link here and a LinkRole there.
The entry point being linked to. Deliberately not sealed: real targets also carry schema:httpMethod, schema:urlTemplate, schema:contentType and domain-specific properties, and JSON-LD is open-world.
registered MIME types are expected

How the target relates to the subject, as a controlled-vocabulary value or a plain string label. Required: a typed link whose relationship is unstated carries no more information than a bare URL, which is what schemaorgProperties/labeledLink is for.
Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.
Component type classification.
Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.
Date the instrument was commissioned (ISO 8601).

Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on an analysis-event instrument (an activity's schema:instrument) they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.

A value fixed by the procedure, where the parameter is NOT overridable. Both keys are declared because both occur: measured across the geochemBuildingBlocks corpus on 2026-10-09, of 369 PropertyValueSpecification entries under schema:instrument, 203 carry schema:defaultValue and 166 carry schema:value. A specification that pins a value rather than defaulting one is still a specification.
Human-readable label for the parameter.
Guidance text for the parameter, e.g. shown beside a form control.

The overridable default this specification carries -- the value that applies unless the analysis overrides it. Left untyped: a default may be a string, a number or a boolean, and which one is a property of the parameter rather than of this shape.
Machine-readable name for the parameter, for serialization and for binding a form control to it.
identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.
Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.
string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.
additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource
identifier for person, recommend ORCID
other labels by which the person might be known. A list when there are several; a single label may be a plain string, as JSON-LD framing writes a one-item list.
if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

An email address or a contact web page (a form, an issue tracker), or both; at least one is required. Schema.org also allows telephone and postal contacts. A URL-only contact is ordinary in DCAT (a vcard:Kind with only vcard:hasURL), so requiring email made such records invalid.
other identifiers for the person
Organization that owns this instrument.
Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.
Product model information for this instrument.
Model identifier.
Model name or number.
Organization that manufactured this instrument.
other identifiers for the organization
identifier for organization
additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource
other labels by which the organization might be known. A list when there are several; a single label may be a plain string, as JSON-LD framing writes a one-item list.
string label for organization that is meaningful for human users
Landing page URL for this instrument.
Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).
Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.
Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.
Human-readable name for this instrument.
Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).

Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.
identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'
Either a bounding box or a point location.

A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.
Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.
Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).
A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.
Ordered steps in this methodology

Sub-procedure for this step, a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use it for a step whose internal procedure has several phases. An {@id} reference names a HowTo described elsewhere in the document or outside it: a sub-procedure several steps share, or one a framed document cuts to its @id where the procedures refer to each other.
The parameter values this step used (e.g. beam conditions for an acquisition step, correction settings for a processing step).
Output entity (or entities) this step produced, which a later step may name as its schema:object.
Input entity (or entities) for this step. Supports chaining, where the value references what a prior step produced.

Instruments, software and reagents this step used, in the same form as the activity's schema:instrument -- either an {@id} reference, or a description in place whose schema:additionalType carries exactly one of the three Wikidata kind terms that selects its shape.
Agent responsible for carrying out this step
Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for a wet-lab step, schema:CreateAction for a step that produces something).
Ordinal position of this step
URL to documentation for this step
Description of what this step involves
Name of this step
The plan this procedure was based on, when the activity both followed a plan and records the procedure as performed. A reference only, for now.
URL to a published methodology or protocol document
Description of the methodology
Name of the methodology or protocol
